headline: Blackhawks’ Patrick Kane activated from IR, expected to return vs. Sabres
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Blackhawks have activated Patrick Kane from injured reserve and expect him back against the Sabres, after he missed the last few games with an upper-body injury. The Athletic's Scott Powers posted that Kane was skating with Andrew Mangiapane and Anton Frondell on a line yesterday.

The return comes with a team that badly needs a lift. CHI is 4-13-1, and our numbers put them at 41.8% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, so they have been outplayed more often than not. Kane's own season is quiet: one goal and eight assists in 15 games, with 3.12 expected goals, so he is about two goals short of what his chances should have produced. That gap looks like bad finishing luck more than a collapse. His 35.47% expected goal share at five-on-five and a team share that drops 6.85 points with him on the ice say CHI has still been pushed back when he plays. In the three games without him, Ryan Donato took his spot beside Nazar and Moore, Artyom Levshunov moved onto the first power-play unit, and Mangiapane rose to 12:39 a night from 10:38. We'd expect that to change now that Kane is back.
